cohort: The study participants were pregnant women at high obstetric risk with a diagnosis of placenta previa, between 20-40 weeks of gestation, with diverse parity and a history of cesarean section.
finding: Specific ultrasound findings (placental heterogenicity and hyperechogenicity, hyperechogenic and irregular chorionic plaque, and hypervascularity) and a Doppler peak flow velocity above 50 cm/sec were found to be highly significant in predicting placental accretism, with a history of second and third cesarean sections also significantly increasing risk.
